summary: Defines the IBM Extended BCD Interchange Code (EBCDIC) and its mapping to ASCII so that every ARPANET host translates between the two in the same way. It describes the 8-bit EBCDIC character set and the extra characters needed.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC presents ways to map characters between ASCII and EBCDIC. It asks sites that use EBCDIC to comment so the network can consider a consistent mapping.

subtitle: Proposed ways for ARPANET sites to map ASCII characters to EBCDIC.

tldr.problem: Sites using ASCII and EBCDIC need a consistent way to translate characters when exchanging data.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes EBCDIC code groups and presents IBM, publishing and graphical approaches to mapping ASCII graphics, with suggested TELNET control codes.
tldr.outcome: The author asks EBCDIC-using sites to comment on the proposed mappings and standard code.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 183 as Unknown and records no RFC that updates or obsoletes it. The text is a proposal for consistent EBCDIC-to-ASCII correspondence and requests comments from sites.

sections.title: The Character Mapping Task
sections.content:
EBCDIC is an 8-bit code used by IBM systems. The RFC's goal is to map ASCII codes to corresponding EBCDIC codes consistently across the ARPA Network.

The basic EBCDIC code includes 54 controls, including space, and 88 graphics. It also has special graphics and a publishing and printing option. For some ASCII graphics, more than one EBCDIC correspondence is possible.
sections.plainLanguage: ASCII and EBCDIC assign codes to characters in different ways. This RFC lays out possible matches so sites can translate text consistently.

sections.title: Three Mapping Approaches
sections.content:
The RFC describes three approaches to mapping ASCII graphics: IBM's recommended correspondences, a publishing correspondence using printing graphics, and a graphical correspondence based on visual similarity. The choices differ for characters that have no direct match or have several plausible matches.

The document also lists EBCDIC control functions and proposes TELNET codes for sync, break, NOP, return to ASCII, echo, no echo and hidden input.
sections.plainLanguage: The three approaches choose different EBCDIC characters for some ASCII symbols. The RFC also suggests codes for TELNET control actions when using EBCDIC.

sections.title: Request for Site Comments
sections.content:
The author asks sites whose operating systems use EBCDIC which mapping they prefer: IBM, publishing, graphical or another correspondence. The questionnaire also asks whether they agree with the proposed standard EBCDIC code, including TELNET control codes.

Sites are asked to report characters or controls that are missing, assigned differently or given special actions by their operating systems.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asks EBCDIC sites to choose a mapping and report differences in their systems. The RFC records a request for feedback, not a final resolution of that request.
